\section{Summary}
What the demo shows:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{The failure is silent.} On the same evo-t2s machine and the same models, the Intel CPU device makes
  Ollama load a 4096-token window and every session loses a rule after the window fills, while the iGPU loads 32768;
  no call surfaces an error. On evo-x2 the qwen3:14b wrong-task rate rises from the default window to 4096 with every
  wrong result returned as a normal answer (view A, Table~\ref{tab:a}).
\item \textbf{The obvious fixes do not hold.} num\_keep reduces but does not remove the wrong-task excess; client-side
  trimming breaks a rule the untrimmed run kept; rule loss depends on the model (story step 2).
\item \textbf{The tool picks the setting per device and model}, and labels every field measured, pending
  flash-attention control or not measured (view B, Table~\ref{tab:b}).
\item \textbf{The money:} fixing a wrong answer in the cloud is cheap (measured redo of every wrong task), sending a
  whole long agent task to the cloud is not (priced from traces); the cost of the failure is that it is silent
  (view C, Table~\ref{tab:c}).
\item \textbf{One live escalation} of a real wrong task through the capped client, with the recorded redo of the same
  task as the fallback (view D, Table~\ref{tab:d}).
\end{itemize}
What it deliberately does not claim:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{No router savings.} The register row b5-verdict is refuted on evo-x2 (the router policy was dominated), so
  no savings figure is shown anywhere, including the older recommendation screen.
\item \textbf{No cloud fix rate.} How many redone tasks the cloud got right is under diagnosis; it is not shown, and the
  clause is withheld from the click-through register row.
\item \textbf{Flash attention versus KV precision is pending.} The fastest measured evo-x2 settings switch flash
  attention on together with q8\_0 / q4\_0; the control that separates them (b5-fa-control) has not read, so those
  fields are labelled pending flash-attention control. Once it reads, view B follows the reading automatically.
\end{itemize}

\section{Story mode}
The dashboard opens in story mode: five steps of about a minute each with Back and Next, a step indicator and
``Explore freely'' (Figures~\ref{fig:s1} to \ref{fig:s5}). Steps 1 to 4 run from the cache; step 5 alone can use the
network, and falls back to the recorded redo. A three-minute backup recording of story mode (no audio, recorded redo
in step 5) is \texttt{demo/review/demo\_story.webm}; the two-page leave-behind is
\texttt{demo/review/LEAVE\_BEHIND.pdf}.
